title: CS1 refute questions from buggy student code
summary: Students receive a programming task and a plausible but incorrect code fragment, then provide a counterexample input that demonstrates the mismatch. The item format develops code comprehension and critique skills needed to evaluate plausible but faulty code, including code produced by generative AI.

sources.title: A Bug's New Life: Creating Refute Questions from Filtered CS1 Student Code Snapshots
sources.evidence_quote: A Refute question presents students with code that fails to achieve a stated task. Students must provide a counter-example input.

assessment.summary: Find an input that proves a supplied buggy implementation does not satisfy its stated programming task.
student_actions: Comprehend the task and supplied code.
Trace the code and produce a counterexample input.

student_role.description: AI is not part of the reported student workflow; the format prepares students to critique plausible faulty code such as LLM output.

assessment_system_role: Buggy historical student submissions are filtered to seed assessment items.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.
